strategies.name: vwap_trend_continuation_retest
strategies.entry_summary: In a directional session bias, wait for price to extend away from VWAP into at least the first, preferably the second, standard-deviation band, then enter in the direction of the session after price breaks back through that band level and retests it. The example given is a long after price moves up,
strategies.exit_summary: Use the second and third standard-deviation bands as profit targets. No explicit stop-loss rule is taught beyond the retest structure, so the runnable exit taught is the band-based target progression.

variants.variant_label: long bias continuation from upper-band retest
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for price to reach first or second standard deviation, then break and retest before entering with the long idea
variants.target_note: use second and third standard deviations as targets
variants.transcript_quote: say you might have a long idea for your session and as the New York session opens ... after we broke it and tested it we can try our long trade this c

variants.variant_label: short bias continuation from lower-band retest
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: same skeleton in the opposite direction for a short-biased session after extension into lower deviations and reaction at
variants.target_note: use outer standard-deviation bands as targets
variants.transcript_quote: we opened the session we shorted the out of the market we went down into the lower standard deviations and here is where you want to look for a trade

strategies.name: vwap_mean_reversion_from_outer_bands
strategies.entry_summary: Use the outer VWAP standard-deviation bands as overbought/oversold levels for reversal trades. Enter when price reaches an outer band area, betting on rebalancing back toward fair value rather than continuation away from it.
strategies.exit_summary: Target the central VWAP as the rebalancing objective. The speaker explicitly presents VWAP itself as the take-profit target for this reversal idea.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: use first/second/third standard-deviation extremes as overbought or oversold references
variants.target_note: central VWAP target for price rebalancing
variants.transcript_quote: if you're using reversal strategies you might want to use these as some sort of overbought or oversold levels ... and use the central vwap as a target

result.enumeration_note: Two distinct executable skeletons are taught: a continuation/retest trade in a session bias, and an opposite mean-reversion trade from outer VWAP bands back to VWAP; opposite logic requires separate strategies.
